card.name: Verbs just before their complement
card.fires_on: Verbs, auxiliaries or particles right after a subject, where the clause's main content comes next, such as 'has resulted', 'appeared to', 'is no more', 'set up'. It is seen in both medical and general web text.

modes.label: Verb after 'has'
modes.description: Past participle such as 'resulted' following 'has', before 'in'.
modes.example: Atrioventricular Blocks Initiation of fingolimod treatment has<< resulted>> in transient AV conduction delays.

modes.label: Linking verb or particle
modes.description: 'is', 'to', 'set' or 'open' that starts a predicate and is followed by its complement.

modes.label: Word closing a noun phrase
modes.description: A participle or preposition such as 'listed', 'for' or 'ago' that ends a phrase and leads into the next clause.
